senses.gloss: the law (Ex. XXXV, 3) forbidding the kindling of fire on the Sabbath.
units: <cite ref="Shabbat 70a:5">Sabb. 70ᵃ</cite> <he>ה׳ ללאו יצאת</he> the law, ‘ye shall kindle no fire &c.’ is singled out in order to indicate that its transgression is a plain offence (<cite ref="L00009"><he>לַאו</he></cite>).

<cite ref="Shabbat 70a:5">Ib.</cite> <he>ה׳ לחלק יצאת</he> that law is specified in order to intimate that each transgression of a Sabbath law is to be atoned for separately (if several of them have been committed in one act); <cite ref="Pesachim 5b:1">Pes. 5ᵇ</cite>.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 2:5:6">Y. Sabb. II, 5ᵃ</cite> bot.; a. fr.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin 7:3:2">Y. Snh. VII, 24ᵇ</cite> bot. we read here (<cite ref="Deuteronomy 19:19">Deut. XIX, 19</cite>) <he>ובערת</he>, and there (ib. XXI, 9) <he>תבער</he>, <he>ה׳ ה׳ וכ׳</he> compare the analogous expressions for analogous modes of execution &c.
<cite ref="Pesikta Rabbati 16:1">Pesik. R. s. 16</cite>, end <he>כדי ה׳ אחת</he> sufficient for one altar fire: Tanḥ. Ki Thissa 10.
